items.stem: A lookup must return a value from a column to the LEFT of the key column and show 'Not found' when there is no match. Which is the best choice?

options.rationale: Correct: XLOOKUP looks in any direction and has a built-in if_not_found argument for missing matches.
VLOOKUP cannot look to the left of its lookup column and has no built-in not-found message.
HLOOKUP searches across rows, not the vertical left-column case described, and also lacks a not-found argument.

options.text: A nested IF chain over every value
options.rationale: A hand-written IF chain does not scale and is error-prone compared with a lookup function.

items.explanation: Correct: XLOOKUP looks in any direction and has a built-in if_not_found argument for missing matches.

items.stem: Which are advantages of cleaning data with Power Query rather than editing cells by hand? (Select TWO)

options.text: The steps are recorded and re-run automatically when new data arrives
options.rationale: Correct: Power Query records each transform so a refresh reapplies them to new data.

options.text: The original source is left unchanged while the query produces the clean output
options.rationale: Correct: the query reads the source and outputs a transformed copy, preserving the source.

options.text: It permanently overwrites the source file so the mess cannot return
options.rationale: Power Query does not overwrite the source; it transforms a loaded copy.

options.text: It guarantees the statistics will be correct without any analysis choices
options.rationale: Cleaning shapes data but does not make analytical decisions correct on its own.

items.explanation: Correct: Power Query records each transform so a refresh reapplies them to new data.; Correct: the query reads the source and outputs a transformed copy, preserving the source.

items.stem: Why add a separate calendar table and relate it to the sales table in the data model?

options.text: It enables time-based measures and avoids duplicating date logic across the model
options.rationale: Correct: a dedicated calendar table gives consistent, reusable time intelligence through the relationship.

options.text: It makes the workbook file smaller in every case
options.rationale: Adding a table does not reliably shrink the file; that is not its purpose.

options.text: It is required before you can type any formula in Excel
options.rationale: Ordinary formulas work without a data model; the calendar table is about modelled analysis.

options.text: It converts text dates to numbers automatically everywhere
options.rationale: Type conversion is a separate cleaning step, not the reason for a related calendar table.

items.explanation: Correct: a dedicated calendar table gives consistent, reusable time intelligence through the relationship.
